My land is in the North China Plain. My father grew wheat and corn here. His father grew wheat and corn here. I have grown wheat and corn here for fifty years. I know this land. I do not need to think about what to grow — there is only one answer.

I have 6 mu of contracted land. I am old. My back is not what it was. My son works in Handan city. I manage alone with some help from my nephew at planting and harvest. 6 mu is what I can handle.

**Winter wheat first.** I plant in October after the rains. I buy my seed from the township supply cooperative — the improved variety, the one everyone around here uses now. I stopped saving my own seed years ago when the cooperative seed started giving better harvests. I rotary-till the field after I pull the corn stalks. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then spread urea at jointing in April. I water four times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once when it heads, once when the grain is filling. I spray once for aphids in May. I harvest in June. I expect around 430 jin per mu. Some years more, some years less.

**Then summer corn on the same ground.** Right after wheat harvest, I plant hybrid corn seed — the kind in the yellow bag, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has. I do not till. The ground is already loose enough and I am tired. I put fertilizer down twice. If August is dry I pump water twice from the village well. I spray once if I see worms. I harvest in September before the rains get cold.

This is my year. It is the same as last year. It is the same as the year before.
